title: BRIDGE: Predicting Human Task Completion Time From Model Performance

split.decision: METR grouped 80/20 family holdout: GroupShuffleSplit(test_size=0.2, random_state=20261030), 142 train tasks/28 validation tasks; 40/10 task families. IRT auxiliary non-target tasks retained without human times. Original 500 evaluation tasks isolated; all archived response cells and test truths verified exactly. Original source task-table row IDs; files sorted by ID. Joint IRT refit during predict on training context + current input, calibration exclusively on train times.

baseline.paper_ref: Figure 3 BRIDGE; reproduced seed-0 accuracy 41.6%; thresholds linear weighted kappa >=0.22 and macro F1 >=0.27.

allowed_changes: completion-time estimators, task/model representations, calibration functions and training surrogate losses
optimization and joint fitting on the current unlabeled batch within the allowed transductive protocol
When retaining the supplied IRT pipeline, changing only epochs=1000 or priors=hierarchical does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Predict human task completion minutes from the supplied sparse model success/failure observations and transfer calibration, maximizing the original four-bucket accuracy with kappa/F1 guards.
supplied binary response observations and missingness, labeled calibration/auxiliary sets and family-disjoint development split
human-time target and transfer setting, right-closed four-bucket definition, weighted-kappa/F1 constraints and no cross-call retention
